newsitem.title: INDIA: India's ONGC's 96/97 output to fall below target.
newsitem.headline: India's ONGC's 96/97 output to fall below target.

text.p: India's Oil and Natural Gas Corporation (ONGC) is expected to produce 29 million tonnes of crude in 1996/97 (April-March) against a target of 31 million for the year, the Press Trust of India (PTI) said on Friday.
PTI quoted ONGC chairman B.C. Bora as saying that technical problems had led to slippages in crude production.
Bora told reporters that out of 400 wells located mostly in the western offshore, 150 wells had been shut for repairs or maintenance leading to production shortfalls.
He said it would take sometime for these wells to resume production.
ONGC produced 31.63 million tonne of crude in 1995/96, up from 29.35 million in 1994/95.
Bora said Bombay High wells might not be able to keep up to their peak production levels.
He said ONGC had already started deep water exploration and drill beyond 300 to 400 metre sea level depths in the eastern and western coast.
"Once we discover oil then it would take enormous investments to take it out," PTI quoted Bora as saying.
Bora said the global trend now was to depend more on natural gas to meet energy needs rather than on liquid fuels, which were depleting.
